title: The Lie derivative, the Frobenius theorem and foliations
summary: Canonical forms for vector fields and the Lie derivative (§21.1); involutive distributions and the Frobenius integrability theorem (Theorem 21.4); foliations, codimension-one foliations and their normal vectors, holonomy of a loop in a leaf, Reeb's stability theorem.

objectives.description: Compute Lie brackets and Lie derivatives using local flows with a consistent sign convention.
Prove the constant-rank Frobenius theorem by commuting adapted vector fields and distinguish integral leaves from embedded submanifolds.
Use the codimension-one criterion, compute holonomy in a suspension example, and state the scope of local and global Reeb stability.

preparation.description: Read lecture 29: §21 canonical forms and §21.1 the Lie derivative, Theorem 21.3.
Read lecture 30: §21.2 the Frobenius integrability theorem (Theorem 21.4), §21.3 foliations (Definition 21.5), §22 codimension-one foliations, §23 holonomy, §24 Reeb's stability theorem.
Read Hitchin §4.3 (one-parameter groups of diffeomorphisms) as preparation for the Lie derivative.

activities.title: Return without the scaffolding
activities.instructions: After a gap, reconstruct the central argument without notes and revisit the transfer or synthesis problem. Compare against your previous work only afterwards. Record what remains unresolved; reading or recall alone does not certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to sample the listed objectives. Give an independent account of the main theorem and its hypotheses, and solve the transfer/synthesis task. An accepted single exercise is evidence only for its tested capabilities, not whole-unit mastery.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Frobenius says every leaf is an embedded submanifold.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Leaves are immersed with an intrinsic topology; an irrational line on a torus is dense and is not embedded.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Local product charts force a compact leaf to have a product neighbourhood.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Holonomy can obstruct a saturated product neighbourhood. Local Reeb stability needs finite holonomy in addition to compactness.
